extracted.intended_audience: market participants, exchange members, aviation industry stakeholders, and public commenters invited to respond to Federal Register notices
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards applicable to submitting and evaluating public comments on a self-regulatory organization fee rule filing and multiple FAA information-collection renewal notices. Covers what evidence and topics the filer/agency uses to justify changes and what commenters are invited to address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonableness of proposed fee based on market comparators
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed fee should be shown reasonable by comparison to competitors' pricing and the value provided (e.g., the Exchange compares its $8,500 per port per month for a 10 Gb physical port to MIAX Pearl’s $8,000 and emphasizes that a single Exchange port provides access to multiple affiliated exchanges and a larger share of the U.S. equities market).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide market-comparator pricing and show how the Exchange’s offering (single physical port connecting to affiliated equities and options exchanges) yields greater market access/value than comparators. Use concrete percentages/market-share comparisons (the filing cites ~11% vs ~1% of U.S. Equities Market) to support claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of an industry-specific PPI (Data PPI) to justify inflation-based increases
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange uses an industry- and product-specific Producer Price Index — Data Processing, Hosting and Related Services (NAICS 518210) and the more granular service line for Hosting, ASP and other IT Infrastructure Provisioning Services — as the inflation metric to guide the proposed price increase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose an index or group of indexes that represent the cost of providing the particular product/service rather than a broad consumer index. Explain NAICS mapping and why the Data PPI specifically reflects the Exchange’s business (hosting, provisioning IT infrastructure, proprietary software usage). Cite BLS factsheets/time series where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure inflation over an appropriate historical period (seven-year cumulative change)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange references historical Data PPI values (starting value in June 2018 and ending value in January 2025) showing a ~16% increase over the period to justify the proposed fee increase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using an index to justify a fee change, present the relevant start/end index values, the cumulative percentage change, and the choice of the period (the filing emphasizes the seven-year span since the last fee change). Explain why cumulative/ multi-year change is an appropriate reference rather than short-term swings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate investments and service improvements that support the fee increase
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange documents infrastructure investments and operational improvements (multi-year platform performance initiative, switch hardware upgrades increasing determinism and capacity ~50%, doubled network bandwidth, new data center NY6, portal improvements, proactive weekly cross-connect audits, latency equalization) as support for the proposed fee increase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete descriptions of capital and operating expenditures, the performance/quality improvements achieved (throughput, processing speed, capacity), and state whether costs have been recouped. Explain how investments benefit members and justify partial recoupment via fee increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable and non-discriminatory assessment of fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed fee is represented as reasonable, equitable, and not unfairly discriminatory because it is assessed uniformly across all market participants purchasing the 10 Gb port, and a single fee applies even when the same port accesses multiple affiliated exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show uniform application across similarly situated participants, explain single-charge treatment for multi-exchange access, and demonstrate no favoritism among categories of market participants (provide examples of how fees are charged in multi-affiliate contexts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of burden on competition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange asserts the proposed change will not impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate, explaining it will not affect intramarket competition (applies equally), will not be a barrier to entry (1 Gb option and third-party resellers remain), and that pricing allocation reflects network resources consumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating competitive effects, analyze (a) whether fees apply equally to similarly situated firms, (b) alternatives for smaller participants (lower-capacity ports or third-party access), and (c) whether the allocation corresponds to resource usage (e.g., 10 Gb ports consume more network resources).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for objective, stable, low-volatility metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange argues Data PPI is appropriate because it is a stable metric with limited volatility (historical calendar-year increases under 2.16% and average change .62% from Jan 2002–Dec 2023) compared to more volatile consumer metrics like CPI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support index choice with volatility comparisons and long-run behavior. Explain why reduced volatility is desirable for contract/fee adjustments, and how it avoids large short-term swings that might trigger other obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirements for submitting comments to the Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested persons may submit written data, views, and arguments by methods listed: Commission’s internet comment form, email to rule-comments@sec.gov (include file number SR-CboeEDGX-2025-041), or by paper comments in triplicate to the SEC Secretary. Use only one method; do not include personal identifiable information; comments will be posted to SEC website and may be redacted or withheld if obscene or copyrighted. Comments due by June 12, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the file number on the subject line for email and reference it in paper submissions. Prefer a single submission method to aid processing. Avoid submitting PII you do not want published; be aware the Commission may withhold or redact certain material under FOIA/5 U.S.C. 552 exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment topics invited for FAA information collections
rubrics_metrics.description: For FAA info-collection renewals, commenters are specifically asked to address: (a) whether the proposed collection is necessary for FAA’s performance; (b) the accuracy of the estimated burden; (c) ways to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information collection; and (d) ways the burden could be minimized without reducing the quality of the collected information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize comments to explicitly address each of the four points. Provide evidence or alternatives when challenging necessity or burden estimates; propose concrete methods to reduce burden (forms consolidation, electronic submission, streamlined fields) while preserving data quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions and benefits to be described for the SAS External Portal
rubrics_metrics.description: The SAS external portal is described by function (submitting PASI, repair station applications FAA Form 8310-3, maintenance school applications FAA Form 8310-6, letters of intent, Element Design DCTs, and sharing other documentation) and benefits (ease of submission, expedited processing/tracking, direct delivery to FS employees eliminating wait time, access to DCTs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When commenting on the portal, reference specific forms/functions and weigh claimed benefits (time savings, direct routing) against any implementation or privacy concerns. Provide suggestions to improve utility/clarity or reduce burden for applicants and certificate holders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required collection content for SAS portal submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Collection information generally includes business name, address, management personnel, type of certificate/rating, aircraft information (if applicable), and a synopsis of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters can evaluate whether each data element is necessary, suggest consolidation or reduction of fields, and propose clarity improvements for how each field should be completed to reduce respondent burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent population and burden estimates should be evaluated
rubrics_metrics.description: Each notice provides respondent counts, frequency, estimated average burden per response (e.g., SAS portal: applicants 1 hour, certificate holders 1.5 hours), and estimated total annual burden and cost figures. The FAA invites comments on accuracy of these estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide empirical data or examples to support alternative burden estimates (time studies, sample form completion times). If suggesting a different estimate, justify with sampling methodology or comparable programs; explain how burden calculations affect OMB clearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary reporting and minimal-necessary-information principle for Suspected Unapproved Parts (FAA Form 8120-11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting of suspected unapproved parts is voluntary; information collected is used to determine whether investigation is warranted and, if confirmed, to issue alerts/notifications. The FAA states any burden is minimized by requesting only necessary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When commenting, address whether the form requests the minimal information required to initiate an investigation, and suggest specific deletions or rewordings to reduce respondent time while preserving investigatory usefulness. Cite potential consequences of under- or over-collection of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information collection to ensure regulatory compliance (Fractional Ownership Programs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information collected from fractional ownership program managers and owners is used to determine compliance with 14 CFR part 91, subpart K and to evaluate program effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should assess whether the requested information is tailored to assure compliance and program evaluation, and recommend any changes to improve clarity, reduce redundant reporting, or better target oversight needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information required for Aviation Insurance collections
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection involves obtaining information from air carriers to establish legally binding aviation war risk insurance policies with the FAA — necessary to determine eligibility, coverage amounts, populate policies, and meet policy conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating these requirements, commenters should consider whether the scope/detail of information requested is necessary for underwriting/coverage decisions, propose ways to streamline data capture, and comment on the estimated burden and frequency of submissions.
